problem_type: Paid intent identity recreated by repeated tool calls
symptom: A model trial reports submission_unknown, then another tool call submits a second provider order.
direct_cause: Every call minted a new node and spend grant; the single-grant attempt limit did not span calls.
class_root: App-scoped paid callers lacked a durable intent claim before approval or dispatch.
affected_population: Model trials across callers, changed prompts/parameters/modes, provider-card revisions and host restarts
entry_points: Repeated and concurrent callers sharing the same app execution root

external_sources.purpose: Separate operation identity from request parameters; preserve a prior outcome.
Stable client identity prevents repeated resource creation across requests.
Do not assume a provider honors idempotency; no blind replay of an unknown POST.

invariants: An unresolved intent is claimed before any await or spend-grant creation.
Same model trial intent always observes the original attempt until an explicit new attempt request passes human confirmation.
Only shared never-sent or explicit-rejection evidence permits one durable retry; changing parameters does not unlock unknown submissions.
The tool receipt and permission to present a new-order confirmation derive from the same persisted record.

door_reduction.why_not: The trial dispatch is the app entry. Type readers describe the same API. Run-owned and project generation callers keep distinct orchestration responsibilities but share submissionOutbox; submissionActions is the receipt/permission projection.

generality_proof: Identity depends on the app execution root and connection/model, never caller, prompt, mode or card revision. The short existing Run lease serializes identity allocation. Every existing job is observation-only after restart, including authorized jobs whose owner crashed. Shared repository/outbox states retain unknown and accepted submissions. Safe retries and explicit new requests allocate journaled jobs and cannot reset their retry/confirmation lineage.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own durable identity allocation and route all app trial submissions through the existing Run outbox.
Project allowed actions for tool receipts and confirmation decisions.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: All model.onboarding.try calls invoke tryModel, which claims before minting a spend grant.
Existing project generation already owns stable Run/job identities and the same shared submissionOutbox; its default safe retry behavior is retained.

recurrence.reason: Any provider or host can lose a paid submission response and repeat the tool call.
same_class_scan: door-map tryModel and follow dispatchModelOnboarding -> dispatcher
door-map createSubmissionOutbox and inspect both generationSubmission and productionGenerationSubmission
Inspect runtime runTask mapped/custom/audio/fallback submit entries and shared outboundDispatchEvidence

prevention.invariant: No app trial dispatch occurs without owning a durable claim; existing unresolved attempts are only observed.
prevention.failure_mode: Unknown, stale request and inaccessible/corrupt persistence never allocate a new provider order.
prevention.strategy: Replace per-call minted identities with shared Run identity/receipt, retaining bounded safe retry and mandatory human confirmation lineage for explicit new attempts.

legacy_paths.rationale: Removed the Date.now-based per-call identity and the unstructured connection-failure decision path; all trial dispatches now claim the Run-owned submission first.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Reuse existing Run repository, lease and outbox; no new durable-execution dependency or custom outbox.

migration: Old per-call trials did not persist an intent identity and cannot be reconstructed without provider evidence. New persisted identities fail closed on missing/corrupt receipts; existing Run records and provider contracts are unchanged.
residual_risks: Real paid verification is reserved for coordination; this line prepares the runner only.
No provider exactly-once guarantee is inferred. Pre-upgrade unknown calls without a durable identity cannot be reconstructed automatically.
Independent acceptance and Windows execution remain unverified by this implementation line.
